extracted.intended_audience: NIH extramural research community (investigators, applicants, program and grants administrators)
extracted.subtask_description: A news/announcement digest summarizing recent NIH policy, process, and resource updates relevant to grant applicants and awardees (e.g., data management formats, review-process changes, initiatives on reproducibility). Meant to inform behavior when preparing applications and managing awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select research models appropriate to research questions
rubrics_metrics.description: "Investigators should still select the models most appropriate for their specific research questions." (in context of New Approach Methodologies, NAMs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH supports a wide range of scientifically sound approaches, including NAMs, that enhance human relevance and translational potential; however, the overarching criterion is appropriateness to the scientific question rather than adopting a specific model type. Use models that best answer the hypothesis and justify choices in applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow PF5 application format and expect linked awards
rubrics_metrics.description: New Video Overview for NIH’s Collaborative International Research Projects (PF5) explains key features and application format and notes that applications may be split into linked awards after review and before Just-in-Time requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should learn the PF5-specific application format and be aware of the procedural possibility that a submitted application can be administratively split into linked awards post-review; prepare proposals and budgets with this possibility and the PF5 format requirements in mind.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the 2026 Pilot Data Management & Sharing (DMS) Plan format
rubrics_metrics.description: A new 2026 Pilot DMS Plan format is available based on a simplified set of required elements to use when preparing Data Management and Sharing Plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When preparing DMS plans for applicable submissions, use the new pilot format and include the simplified required elements. Check the issued resource for the exact elements and structure to ensure compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embed replication and reproducibility across research and applications
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH’s Gold Standard Science plan advances a commitment to replication and reproducibility and NIH launched a Replication and Reproducibility Initiative to drive, incentivize, and institutionalize these efforts across the biomedical research enterprise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants and awardees should incorporate measures that support reproducibility (e.g., experimental design, replication plans, transparent methods/data sharing) into applications and project plans; expect reproducibility to be a highlighted consideration in review and funding decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand 'Competitive But Not Discussed' (CBND) designation and triage thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: Following emergency modifications, the middle third of applications in a study section were designated as “competitive but not discussed” recognizing that strong applications may fall below a 33% cutoff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should be aware of triage practices and that being scored as competitive does not guarantee discussion. Know how your application’s percentile/score relates to discussion thresholds and that policy changes can alter which applications are discussed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Centralized peer review via the Center for Scientific Review (CSR)
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH announced that all peer review would be centralized within the Center for Scientific Review (CSR) to strengthen efficiency, competition, and transparency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Researchers and applicants should expect consolidated review processes, potential changes in study section organization or procedures, and adapt application planning and expectations accordingly. Monitor CSR guidance for specific procedural impacts on application submission and review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be aware of programmatic and administrative updates (e.g., Small Business/Seed Fund)
rubrics_metrics.description: Announcements such as NIH’s Seed Fund being reinstated and schedule notices (e.g., NIH closures, NAC meetings) inform program availability and timing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stay informed of program restarts or changes (which affect eligibility and opportunities) and calendar/administrative notices that influence submission deadlines, institutional planning, and points of contact for program-specific questions.
